alice.support: Hey team, AcmeCorp (ticket #ST-4821) just reported SSO failing right after their IdP rotated certs. They get a 500 on our /saml/acs endpoint. Logs show: 
```
Error: Signature verification failed: certificate thumbprint mismatch
at SamlVerifier.verify (/srv/app/saml/verifier.js:142:21)
Caused by: SamlParserError: no matching X509Certificate found in IdP metadata
```
I pulled their metadata and noticed it's being served with gzip and includes two KeyDescriptor elements where the signing cert appears second (encryption first). Not sure if our metadata fetcher is skipping the second cert or if order matters.

kevin.support: Can you paste the IdP metadata and the ACS/Entity URLs? Also, does this reproduce in our staging? Any recent code pushes? :thinking_face:

alice.support: Here are the key bits (redacted):
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme-corp.com">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="encryption">
      <KeyInfo><ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...ENCRYPTIONCERT==</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <KeyInfo><ds:X509Data><ds:X509Certificate>MIIC...SIGNINGCERT==</ds:X509Certificate></ds:X509Data></KeyInfo>
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
Also `curl -I https://idp.acme-corp.com/metadata` shows `Content-Encoding: gzip`. Our fetcher logs: `Fetched metadata (200), content-encoding: gzip, length: 482` then later `Parsed metadata: 1 entity, 1 signing cert` (so it's detecting only one cert). Repro steps I ran locally: `samltest-tool --metadata https://idp... --acs https://app.redwood.ai/saml/acs --relaystate foo` which failed with same signature error.

devin.identity: Thanks, this looks like a metadata parsing edge case. Two likely issues: 1) our metadata decompression path sometimes strips or munges whitespace/newlines inside the X509Certificate block when Content-Encoding is gzip -> base64 decode fails for the second cert; 2) our parser historically picked the first KeyDescriptor for signing by default and ignored explicit use attributes when multiple descriptors present. I'll dig in.

devin.identity: Quick mitigation we can offer to the customer: either upload the IdP metadata XML manually in the Console (Org -> Security -> SSO -> Upload IdP metadata) or have their IdP publish the signing cert as the first KeyDescriptor temporarily. For an internal fix, I'll add both: robust gzip handling and change parser to collect all ds:X509Certificate values regardless of order and map by use attribute.

maya.security: Please don't enable any "accept unsigned/signing fallback" flag for prod — that's insecure. If we do a temporary bypass for the customer, make it a one-off metadata upload tied to the org and log the exception with TTL. Also add an audit event for manual uploads. :lock:

devin.identity: Agreed. I'll implement parser fix + add audit hooks. Plan: PR with tests that include metadata with multiple KeyDescriptor elements, gzipped and non-gzipped. I'll also add a migration to re-parse cached metadata for orgs with >1 KeyDescriptor. ETA: patch branch by EOD, review tomorrow morning.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued: canary/release-2025.12.8-rc -> infra-staging (owner: devops) :rocket:

devin.identity: PR created: https://git.internal/redwood/identity/pulls/3456 (adds robust metadata decompression + collects all certificates). Requesting review from @maya.security and @owen.platform for perf implications.

maya.security: Reviewing now. Main thing: ensure we don't expand attack surface by accepting multiple certificates from unauthenticated metadata. We should validate certificate subject/issuer and require either the cert thumbprint match in a provided config or org confirmation.

devin.identity: Added an optional fingerprint check step (Console UI will show detected cert fingerprints and require support/owner confirmation before switching signing cert). Tests pass locally.

devin.identity: Merged to main and scheduled canary deploy to staging. Please test with AcmeCorp once staging has the new release.

alice.support: I uploaded the metadata manually for AcmeCorp as a temporary measure and told them to test. They just confirmed SSO works now. :tada: I'll mark the ticket resolved after we push to prod and I can revert the manual upload.

maya.security: Good. After prod deploy, run a short audit on manual uploads in the last 24h and ensure TTLs are set. Also add a note to the runbook for on-call: if metadata parsing fails after cert rotations, try manual upload + request IdP to reissue metadata with clear use attributes.

alice.support: Will follow up post-deploy and confirm. Thanks @devin.identity and @maya.security for the quick turnaround.
